To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overexpression of Cav‐3 in mice protects against the development of heart failure by reducing cellular hypertrophy and preserving t‐tubule‐mediated ICa, but has no effect on t‐tubules Ca2+ release.
overexpression of Cav‐3 preserves t-tubular I Ca but not local t-tubular Ca2 + release in heart failure induced in vivo.
Cav‐3 overexpressed in the heart protects against some of the cellular changes associated with heart failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular basis of the cardiac hypertrophic response and its consequences for Ca2+ handling and contractile function.
the cellular mechanisms that underlie the progression of heart failure in mice following pressure overload.
the role of the caveolae in the pathogenesis of heart failure, and in particular the role of Cav‐3 in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study shows that Cav‐3 over-expression preserves t‐t‐ubular I Ca and prevents hypertrophy during heart failure in vivo, but does not prevent Ca2+ release from the t‐tubule.
the overexpression of Cav‐3 in the heart of mice provides protection against many of the cellular and molecular changes that accompany pressure overload induced heart failure but not against all.
Cav‐3 overexpressing myocytes show reduced hypertrophy and improved t‐tubule I Ca but not t‐tubularr Ca2+ release in heart failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
overexpression of the scaffolding protein Cav‐3 in the heart of mice provides specific, but limited, protection against heart failure.
Cav‐3 overexpressed in heart failure mice can preserve t‐tubules I Ca but not local Ca2+ release and this is not enough to prevent heart failure progression.
Cav‐3 OE has a protective effect on the heart against the development of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cav‐3 OE preserves t‐tubu‐lar Ca2+ influx, and thus Ca2+ cycling, but not local Ca2+ release in heart failure.
overexpression of Cav‐3 preserves t-tubular ICa in heart failure, which is a novel and unexpected finding.
overexpression of Cav‐3 in the heart provides a degree of protection against heart failure induced by chronic pressure overload.
